chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar who said:
I read in a letter of 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! It has been reported from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) placed zakat upon nine things: wheat, barley, dates, raisins, gold, silver, sheep, cattle, and camels; and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) excused [from zakat] whatever was besides that.' So a questioner said to him: 'With us there are many things that are multiples of that.' He said: 'And what is it?' He said to him: 'Rice.' So Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I am telling you that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) placed zakat upon nine things and excused whatever was besides that, and you say: With us there is rice, and with us there is corn — but corn existed in the era of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family)!'

So he (peace be upon him) signed [in response]: 'It is as such; and zakat is upon everything that is measured by the sa'a.' And 'Abdullah wrote: And it is reported by other than this man from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he was asked about grains,

so he said: 'And what are they?' He said: 'Sesame, and rice, and millet — and all of this is produce like wheat and barley.' So Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'On all grains, there is zakat.'

key_terms.الزكاة: Zakat — the obligatory alms-tax on specific forms of wealth
key_terms.الصاع: Al-sa'a — a traditional volumetric dry measure (approximately 3 litres), used as the standard for zakat calculation on grains
key_terms.وضع: Wada'a — established/imposed (referring to the prophetic institution of zakat)
key_terms.وقّع: Waqqa'a — signed/endorsed (referring to the Imam's written response on a petition)

ai.seo_question: Is zakat obligatory on rice, corn, and all grains according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the scope of zakat on agricultural produce and grains. It records a written exchange in which 'Ali ibn Mahziyar reads a letter from 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad to Imam al-Hadi (AS), citing a prior ruling of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that the Prophet established zakat on nine specific items. When questioned about crops like rice and corn that were not mentioned, the Imam firmly upheld the prophetic precedent, and then signed a clarifying response: zakat applies to everything measured by the sa'a. A supplementary narration confirms that all grains — including sesame, rice, and millet — are subject to zakat. This hadith is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it extends zakat beyond the nine explicitly named categories to all grain crops measured by volumetric standards.
